title: ZTF colours show that 0.1-0.7 µm grains, not saturation, make the dips of the old K star Gaia20cdd near-grey; a second old K dimmer has smaller grains, full cover and no infrared excess
abstract: Prior campaign studies found deep dips of the old K-type star Gaia20cdd and explained its near-grey optical colours by saturation of a small-grain screen. We tested this with colour trajectories: the ZTF g depth against the r (and i) depth on the same night, for every dip night of five main-sequence dimmers. We fitted full-screen and partial-cover models with a free optical depth per night, then Mie grain models through the ZTF and WISE filters, with NEOWISE data. For Gaia20cdd the 2022 dip follows one line with k_g = tau(g)/tau(r) = 1.107 (1.096-1.122) from 0.1 to 3.4 mag; interstellar dust gives 1.40. Only 3.8 percent of the light stays uncovered, and it bends the trajectory only below 3 mag. Thus saturation does not make the colours grey. Uncovered light is real over all 175 dip nights (delta 2 lnL = 76; at most 15.9 in 50 full-screen simulations) and changes between episodes (3.8 to 54 percent). Together with the 2022 NEOWISE depths, the colours need n(a) ~ a^-3.5 grains from about 0.05-0.1 to 0.3-0.74 um; distributions down to 0.01-0.03 um are worse by delta chi2 >= 64. The second old K dimmer, Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504, follows one steeper line (k_g = 1.62, 1.61-1.65) from its 2018-2020 faint state to its 2.4 mag (r), 4.2 mag (g) core, with less than 2 percent uncovered light; Mie fits give 0.10-0.23 um silicate grains. Its faint state is real (0.18 mag in r; 39 same-field stars changed by less than 0.05 mag), NEOWISE W1 did not change (-0.019 +- 0.020 mag; a grey occulter is excluded at 15 sigma), and its W1-W2 colour is normal. Silicate grains of these sizes are not blown out by radiation pressure (beta < 0.5). Thus the two deep old-star dimmers have different dust. Limitations: spherical grains of two compositions, one size slope, blackbody stars, one NEOWISE visit for Gaia20cdd (the lower size cut-off needs it), detections-only ZTF data, and no spectra. citations.reason: We use its 2022 NEOWISE depths, W2 excess, dip windows and Mie code. Our colour trajectories show that saturation does not cause the near-grey optical colours of Gaia20cdd; grains without the smallest sizes do. Its small-grain, non-opaque result stays valid.
Discovery of Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504 and its 2018-2020 faint state; we confirm the faint state with comparison stars and add the grain size, covering and infrared results.

Independent NEOWISE kappa values for the dwarf dimmers; our grain fits agree that the occulters are not grey.
